122.canonical: Split or simplify complex boolean expressions to improve testability and comprehension instead of relying solely on expensive structural coverage criteria, while still testing the underlying complexity.

145.canonical: Separate infrastructure and UI/framework code from domain code — using ports and adapters so the domain depends on technology-agnostic interfaces while adapters hold infrastructure detail — so business rules can be tested without external-system concerns.

146.canonical: Keep domain classes cohesive and free of infrastructure and external calls, because single-responsibility, infrastructure-free code is easier to test and avoids testability debt.

155.canonical: Design classes to be loosely coupled and highly cohesive with explicit substitutable dependencies, since only such classes are easy to unit-test; when a test grows large or is hard to write, treat it as a design signal to split the class or introduce abstractions.
